questions.question_text: Find the equation of the curve obtained by reflecting $y = 2x^2 - 5x + 1$ across the $x$-axis.

options.why: Reflected across the y-axis instead of the x-axis.
Negated only the leading quadratic term instead of the entire function.
Applied negative signs inconsistently across terms.

questions.question_text: Find the equation of the curve obtained by reflecting $y = \sqrt{4 - 2x}$ across the $y$-axis.

options.why: Reflected across the x-axis instead of the y-axis.
Reflected across both the x-axis and the y-axis.
Negated the constant term under the square root instead of x.

questions.question_text: Find the equation of the curve resulting from reflecting $y = 5^x - 3$ across both axes (a $180^\circ$ rotation about the origin).

options.why: Negated the exponential term and exponent but forgot to negate the constant term -3.
Reflected only across the y-axis.
Reflected only across the x-axis.

questions.question_text:
The curve $y = 2^{x+3}$ is transformed to $y = 2^{3-x}$.
Which transformation maps the first curve onto the second?

options.why: Confused replacing x by -x with negating the entire function output.

options.text: A rotation of $180^\circ$ about the origin
options.why: Thought both x and y were negated rather than just x.

options.text: A vertical translation of $6$ units down
options.why: Mistook the sign change in the exponent for an additive vertical shift.

questions.solution_text:
In $y = 2^{x+3}$, replacing $x$ by $-x$ gives $y = 2^{-x+3} = 2^{3-x}$.
Replacing $x$ with $-x$ corresponds to a reflection across the $y$-axis.
A reflection across the $y$-axis

questions.question_text:
The graph of $y = f(x)$ has a turning point at $(-3, 8)$.
What are the coordinates of the corresponding turning point on the graph of $y = -f(x)$?

options.why: Reflected across the y-axis instead of the x-axis by negating the x-coordinate.
Negated both coordinates, performing a 180 degree rotation instead of an x-axis reflection.
Swapped the x- and y-coordinates as in a reflection across the line y=x.

questions.solution_text:
A reflection across the $x$-axis transforms $(x, y) \to (x, -y)$.
$(-3, 8) \to (-3, -8)$

questions.question_text:
The graph of $y = \dfrac{1}{x+5}$ has a vertical asymptote at $x = -5$.
Where is the vertical asymptote of the reflected graph $y = f(-x)$?

options.why: Assumed the vertical asymptote position does not change under a y-axis reflection.
Confused the vertical asymptote equation x = c with a horizontal line y = c.
Confused vertical and horizontal asymptotes and did not negate the coordinate.

questions.solution_text:
Under a reflection across the $y$-axis, $x$ is replaced by $-x$.
The vertical asymptote $x = -5$ becomes $-x = -5 \implies x = 5$.

questions.question_text:
A function $g(x)$ satisfies $g(-x) = g(x)$ for all $x$.
If the point $(k, m)$ lies on $y = g(x)$, which other point must also lie on the graph?

options.why: Confused y-axis symmetry with x-axis reflection symmetry.
Applied the property of odd functions with rotational symmetry instead of even functions.
Applied inverse function reflection in the line y = x.

questions.solution_text:
Since $g$ is an even function ($g(-x) = g(x)$), its graph is symmetric about the $y$-axis.
If $(k, m)$ lies on the curve, then $g(k) = m$.
Then $g(-k) = g(k) = m$, so $(-k, m)$ must lie on the graph.

questions.question_text:
The circle $(x - 3)^2 + (y + 4)^2 = 25$ is reflected across both coordinate axes.
What is the equation of the resulting circle?

options.why: Reflected only across the y-axis, changing only the sign of the x-coordinate.
Reflected only across the x-axis, changing only the sign of the y-coordinate.
Swapped the centre coordinates instead of negating them.
